snapshots.name: Pierre
snapshots.subtitle: Count Bezukhov's illegitimate son, newly returned from abroad
snapshots.body: Large, awkward, and out of place among the polished company of a St. Petersburg soiree, he has just come back from years of education in France with opinions his hostess finds alarming. His father's fortune and title are about to change his life considerably.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Prince Andrew Bolkónski
snapshots.subtitle: A discontented young officer, Pierre's closest friend
snapshots.body: Clever, restless, and privately weary of both his marriage and society's chatter, he is about to leave for the army in search of the kind of glory he cannot find at home. His friendship with Pierre is one of the few things he takes entirely seriously.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Natásha
snapshots.subtitle: The lively young daughter of the Rostov family
snapshots.body: Still a girl at her family's name-day party, impulsive and full of feeling in a way her more careful relations are not, she grows up through the novel into the center of several men's hopes. Her warmth draws people to the Rostov household from every side.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Count Rostóv
snapshots.subtitle: Natasha's father, a generous, improvident Moscow nobleman
snapshots.body: Warmhearted and hospitable to a fault, he spends far more than the family's estate can support and leaves its finances in steadily worsening order. His household is nonetheless one of the warmest in Moscow.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Countess Rostóva
snapshots.subtitle: Natasha's mother
snapshots.body: Devoted to her children and increasingly anxious about the family's finances, she manages the Rostov household with more realism than her husband allows himself. Her children's marriages matter to her as much for security as for love.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Nicholas Rostóv
snapshots.subtitle: Natasha's elder brother, a young hussar
snapshots.body: Eager and impressionable, he leaves for the army early in the novel with romantic ideas about war that his first real campaign complicates considerably. His devotion to his regiment and his emperor runs deep.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Sónya
snapshots.subtitle: A poor cousin raised alongside the Rostov children
snapshots.body: Quiet and fiercely loyal, she has grown up in the Rostov household as one of the family without ever quite having a family of her own. Her attachment to Nicholas is the deepest feeling she has.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Pétya
snapshots.subtitle: The youngest Rostov son
snapshots.body: Still a boy for much of the novel, he idolizes his older brother Nicholas and longs for nothing more than to be old enough to join the army himself. His enthusiasm for glory is entirely unclouded by experience.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Véra
snapshots.subtitle: The eldest Rostov daughter
snapshots.body: Correct and rather cold where her siblings are warm, she is generally considered the least charming of the Rostov children. Her engagement to Berg suits her practical temperament.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Berg
snapshots.subtitle: An ambitious, methodical young officer
snapshots.body: Precise to the point of absurdity about his own career and possessions, he courts and eventually marries Vera Rostova. His single-minded self-advancement amuses the rest of the Rostov family more than it impresses them.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Princess Mary Bolkónskaya
snapshots.subtitle: Prince Andrew's plain, devout sister
snapshots.body: Living under her demanding father's roof in the countryside, she finds her chief consolation in religion and in letters from a close friend in Moscow. Her father's temper and her own sense of duty leave her little room for a life of her own.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: old Prince Bolkónski
snapshots.subtitle: Andrew and Mary's father, a retired general
snapshots.body: Exacting, sharp-tongued, and unable to tolerate idleness in himself or anyone near him, he keeps a strict household on his country estate. His children love him without ever quite feeling at ease around him.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Prince Vasíli Kurágin
snapshots.subtitle: A well-connected St. Petersburg courtier
snapshots.body: Smooth, calculating, and always alert to a useful match or a favor worth doing, he takes an active interest in Pierre's sudden inheritance and in placing his own children advantageously. Little he does in society is without a further motive.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Anatole
snapshots.subtitle: Prince Vasili's handsome, reckless son
snapshots.body: Charming, careless with money and with other people's feelings, he drifts through society leaving debts and complications behind him. His good looks open doors his character does nothing to deserve.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Hélène
snapshots.subtitle: Prince Vasili's beautiful daughter
snapshots.body: Celebrated everywhere for her looks and her poise, she becomes entangled with Pierre's life not long after his fortune changes. Her serene surface gives away very little of what she actually wants.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Borís
snapshots.subtitle: The ambitious son of a poor widowed friend of the Rostovs
snapshots.body: Determined to make his way in the world through good connections rather than good luck, he cultivates useful friendships in the army and in society with quiet persistence. His childhood attachment to Natasha does not survive his ambitions.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Dólokhov
snapshots.subtitle: A daring, dangerous officer and gambler
snapshots.body: Fearless in battle and ruthless at the card table, he is a close companion of Anatole's in the wilder side of Moscow society. Few people cross him without regretting it.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Denísov
snapshots.subtitle: Nicholas Rostov's hussar commander and friend
snapshots.body: Blustering, warmhearted, and given to a speech impediment that softens his fierce reputation, he takes young Nicholas Rostov under his wing in the regiment. He later falls under Natasha's spell during a visit to Moscow.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Kutúzov
snapshots.subtitle: The aging Russian commander-in-chief
snapshots.body: Patient, unglamorous, and often distrusted by the younger officers around him, he commands the Russian armies against Napoleon with a fatalism that looks like weakness until events prove otherwise. His calm is deliberate, not accidental.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Napoleon
snapshots.subtitle: The French emperor
snapshots.body: Discussed, admired, and feared across Russian drawing rooms long before he ever appears in the story directly, he embodies the historical current the whole novel moves against. Pierre in particular cannot decide what to make of him.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Karatáev
snapshots.subtitle: A simple peasant soldier Pierre meets as a prisoner
snapshots.body: Round, gentle, and entirely at peace with whatever happens to him, he shares Pierre's captivity and offers him a way of seeing the world that Pierre has never encountered among his own class. His effect on Pierre outlasts their brief acquaintance.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Márya Dmítrievna
snapshots.subtitle: A blunt, formidable family friend of the Rostovs
snapshots.body: Known throughout Moscow for saying exactly what she thinks regardless of rank, she is one of the few people who can speak plainly to the Rostov family in a crisis. Her bluntness comes from real affection, not indifference.
